steps.name: read the request and the code
steps.instructions: Read the request, keel's memory of the project and the code the request touches (grep, open the files it names and their neighbours; edit nothing, write no file, ask nothing yet). Write a short map, at most 40 lines: the files and symbols the request touches (file:line), the pattern nearby to follow (file:line), the stack (language, framework, key libraries), the tests that exist for that code (or none), and what the request and the code already answer (scope, behaviour, errors, numbers, who may do what). Then name the task type the request suggests: feature (New feature: building something that does not exist yet), bug (Bug fix: something is broken), performance (Performance: too slow, hits a deadline, or costs too much), refactor (Refactor: change shape without changing behavior), api (API integration: wire up an external service) or architecture (Architecture: an irreversible decision, pick an approach). And the sections worth running, by number: 1 Requirement questions, 2 Acceptance criteria, 3 Definition of Done, 4 Red-flag check, 5 Ready-to-send prompt, 6 Next-step recommendation. Leave one out only when its skip rule holds: 1 when the requirements are already written and unambiguous, 2 when the request already holds acceptance criteria, 3 for a trivial one-line fix, 4 when the scope is clean, 5 when the work is handed to a spec or plan anyway, 6 when the next step is already known. TASK-TYPE is one of feature, bug, performance, refactor, api, architecture, then a dash and the reason in a few words. SECTIONS is the numbers, comma separated.
